name: Disasters & alerts
desc: Wildfire, storms, heatwaves, high water and dike breaches, long power cuts, evacuation, emergency kit

guides.w: Smoke, flames or an evacuation order
s: Call 112 as soon as you see fire. Follow the authorities' instructions.
Leave early: don't wait until you see flames.
Move away from the fire and against the wind direction, to roads and open ground. Avoid narrow valleys and slopes above the fire.
In a car: windows closed, ventilation off, lights on, drive slowly in smoke.
At home: close windows and doors, remove flammable things near the house, wet cloth over nose and mouth against smoke.
Trapped: go to bare ground, water, or an area that's already burnt.
d: Don't go towards the fire to look
Don't hide in a dead end

s: When you hear thunder, lightning is close enough to hit: go inside a building or a car.
Outside with no shelter: stay away from tall trees, poles, water and hilltops; crouch low on your feet.
Stay inside until 30 minutes after the last thunder.
Strong wind: stay away from windows, trees and scaffolding.
d: Don't shelter under a lone tree
Don't swim or stay on the beach

s: Drink regularly before you're thirsty.
Stay out of the sun 11:00–17:00; plan trips for morning and evening.
Keep rooms cool: shutters closed in the day, windows open at night.
Check on older people and children.
Watch for heat exhaustion (headache, dizziness, nausea): move to a cool place, rest, drink. Confused or very hot: see “Heat stroke”.
d: Never leave anyone in a parked car

s: Leave when told to, by the route given.
Take: phone and charger, power bank, ID and documents, medicines, water, a jacket, cash.
Switch off gas, water and electricity if there's time.
Tell your group where you're going (the app sends texts if there's no internet).
Go to the official reception point or the meeting place you agreed.
d: Don't take shortcuts through closed areas

s: Water: 3 litres per person per day, for at least 3 days.
Food that keeps and needs no cooking: tins (with a hand opener), crackers, nuts, dried fruit, bars.
Torch or head torch, spare batteries, and a battery or wind-up radio.
Power bank (charged), phone cables, and a list of important phone numbers on paper.
First-aid kit, your regular medicines for a week, and spare glasses.
Copies of ID and insurance papers in a waterproof bag, some cash in small notes, spare keys.
Whistle, rain jacket, a warm layer, a blanket or emergency blanket.
Hand gel, wet wipes, bin bags and toilet paper. Things for babies or pets if you have them.
Check it twice a year, for example when the clocks change: replace water, food and batteries.

guides.t: High water or a dike breach
guides.w: The Netherlands: water from rivers or sea
s: Check now on overstroomik.nl whether your address could flood and how deep.
Follow NL-Alert and the regional broadcaster: they tell you whether to leave or to go up.
Told to leave: go early, with your go-bag, medicines and pets. Turn off gas, water and power.
Told to stay: go to the highest floor with water, food, a radio, a torch and warm clothes.
Move valuables and important papers upstairs; sandbags in front of doors slow the water.
Afterwards: don't drink tap water until it's declared safe; have the power checked before switching it on.
d: Don't walk or drive through flood water

s: Keep the fridge and freezer closed: a full freezer stays cold for about 2 days.
Save your phone battery: low-power mode, brightness down. Use a battery radio for news.
Switch off and unplug sensitive devices, but leave one lamp on so you notice when the power comes back.
Cook outside on a camping stove or barbecue, never indoors (carbon monoxide).
In flats, water pumps may stop: fill the bath and bottles while water still runs.
Have cash: card machines and ATMs won't work.
Stay warm in one room (see Staying warm without heating) and use torches rather than candles.
Check on neighbours, especially older people living alone. Agree where your family meets if phones stop working.
d: Never use a barbecue, generator or gas heater indoors
Candles: never leave them burning alone
